newsitem.title: USA: Iraq rebuilt missile base after U.S. attack - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq rebuilt missile base after U.S. attack - paper.

text.p: Iraq rebuilt a surface-to-air missile network in southern Iraq within two weeks of the U.S. cruise missile attack to destroy it, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday.
"It is the same basic (antiaircraft missile system) that was there before the 30th of August 1996," an unidentified senior defence official told the newspaper.

U.S. warships and planes launched 44 cruise missiles against the air defence system on Sept. 2 and 3 in retaliation for Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein's offensive into Kurdish-held territory in northern Iraq.
Since the attack, the Iraqis had not used the radar or their Soviet-made missiles, the Post quoted the official as saying.

But it would take just "a flip of the switch" to turn on the targeting radar and create a threat to U.S. and allied military aircraft patrolling the no-fly zone in southern Iraq, according to the official.
The newspaper said the official added that there was no indication on Baghdad's part "of an intent to challenge" aircraft policing the area off limits to Iraqi planes.
After the U.S. strikes last month, the Clinton administration strongly warned Saddam against rebuilding the fixed missile sites.
